{"concept_id":"drv.interaction.overtake_pass","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear: a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it. b is ahead of a where the longitudinal component of b's bearing in a's frame (rel.bearing) is positive and the two bodies' projections on a's heading share no length (rel.longitudinal_overlap negative); b is behind a where that component is negative and the projections share no length. The act begins at the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of a with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction). The act is recognized at the observation at which b is behind a and was not behind a at the previous observation, where b was ahead of a with headings aligned at some observation of the window behind. The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until b has again been ahead of a and then comes to be behind it. Conduct before the window behind is not read: a pass that takes longer than the window is not recognized. It denotes the relative motion of the two road users only: it says nothing of the lanes they occupy, of whether b moves, or of why a passes. Not denoted: a drawing alongside b that does not clear b; b ahead of a only while their headings are not aligned (a road user met head-on or crossing); b behind a at every observation of the window.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"a","sort":"track"},{"name":"b","sort":"track"}],"params":[{"name":"window","unit":"s","meaning":"the longest duration of a pass the concept recognizes: how far behind the observation it looks for b ahead of a"},{"name":"same_dir_cos","unit":"ratio","meaning":"cosine of the largest heading difference at which a and b count as travelling in the same direction"}],"act":{"boundary":"window","window":"window","onset":"The act begins at the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of a with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction).","recognition":"The act is recognized at the observation at which b is behind a and was not behind a at the previous observation, where b was ahead of a with headings aligned at some observation of the window behind.","extent":"The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until b has again been ahead of a and then comes to be behind it.","history":"Conduct before the window behind is not read: a pass that takes longer than the window is not recognized."},"elements":[{"span":"the longitudinal component of b's bearing in a's frame (rel.bearing)","atoms":["rel.bearing"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.bearing: 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for \"on the right of\", \"immediately to the rear\")'; its longitudinal component's sign tells b ahead of a from b behind it."},{"span":"the two bodies' projections on a's heading share no length (rel.longitudinal_overlap negative)","atoms":["rel.longitudinal_overlap"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.longitudinal_overlap: 'the length the two footprints' projections on that axis share, negative for the gap between the projections'; a negative value means the bodies are not side by side, so a has cleared b (or not yet reached it). Used as a projection, not as a contact or a distance."},{"span":"with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction)","atoms":["rel.same_direction"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.same_direction: 'headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance', with the tolerance same_dir_cos; it tells an overtaking from a meeting or a crossing."}],"residues":[],"literals":[],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"a follows b in the same lane 15 m behind at 12 m/s while b is halted; a moves to the adjacent lane, draws alongside and, 4 s after b was last ahead of it, has b 3 m behind it: at that observation the concept holds."},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"a follows b, moves to the adjacent lane and draws alongside b, then halts with the two bodies still side by side; b never comes to be behind a within the window."},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"a draws past b in the adjacent lane, but the bearing of b from a is not observed.","masked":["rel.bearing"]}],"used_by":["LVMC_11_30_030"],"supersedes":null}

{"concept_id":"drv.motion.moving_across_carrier","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user a moves across the designated direction of travel of carrier region r: a is moving, its speed (kin.speed) above speed_tol, and its velocity (kin.velocity) makes with r's designated direction (st.lane_direction) an angle whose cosine, in absolute value, is at most cos_max: the absolute value of the dot product of the velocity with the normalised direction is at most cos_max times the speed. Either sense of crossing is denoted: the sign of the direction does not matter. It is a state at one observation: it says nothing of whether a occupies r, of where a began or will end its movement, or of how long it has moved so. Not denoted: a road user at rest or moving at or below speed_tol; a road user moving more nearly along r's direction than cos_max allows. Where r carries no designated direction, or a's velocity is not observed, it is unknown.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"a","sort":"track"},{"name":"r","sort":"region"}],"params":[{"name":"speed_tol","unit":"m/s","meaning":"the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement"},{"name":"cos_max","unit":"ratio","meaning":"the largest absolute cosine between the velocity and the carrier's designated direction at which the motion counts as across the carrier"}],"elements":[{"span":"its speed (kin.speed) above speed_tol","atoms":["kin.speed"],"concepts":[],"justification":"kin.speed: 'magnitude of velocity' (m/s); above speed_tol the road user is moving."},{"span":"its velocity (kin.velocity)","atoms":["kin.velocity"],"concepts":[],"justification":"kin.velocity: 'velocity vector' (m/s, world frame); its dot product with the direction gives the motion along the carrier."},{"span":"r's designated direction (st.lane_direction)","atoms":["st.lane_direction"],"concepts":[],"justification":"st.lane_direction: 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in — a lane, ... or a roadway', read normalised; a place no carrier covers has none (unknown)."}],"residues":[],"literals":[],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A pedestrian on a lane whose direction is east walks north at 1.4 m/s: the dot product is zero, at most cos_max times the speed."},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"A pedestrian on the same lane walks east along it at 1.4 m/s: the absolute cosine is 1, above cos_max."},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"A pedestrian on the lane moves, but its velocity is not observed.","masked":["kin.velocity"]}],"used_by":["LVMC_11_30_050","LVMC_11_30_060_A","LVMC_11_30_060_B"],"supersedes":null}

Conduct before the window behind is not read: a pass that takes longer than the window is not recognized. It denotes the relative motion of the two road users only: it says nothing of the lanes they occupy, of whether b moves, or of why a passes. {"concept_id":"drv.motion.moving_across_carrier","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user a moves across the designated direction of travel of carrier region r: a is moving, its speed (kin.speed) above speed_tol, and its velocity (kin.velocity) makes with r's designated direction (st.lane_direction) an angle whose cosine, in absolute value, is at most cos_max: the absolute value of the dot product of the velocity with the normalised direction is at most cos_max times the speed. {"concept_id":"drv.interaction.overtake_pass","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear: a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it. b is ahead of a where the longitudinal component of b's bearing in a's frame (rel.bearing) is positive and the two bodies' projections on a's heading share no length (rel.longitudinal_overlap negative); b is behind a where that component is negative and the projections share no length. The act begins at the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of a with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction). The act is recognized at the observation at which b is behind a and was not behind a at the previous observation, where b was ahead of a with headings aligned at some observation of the window behind. The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until b has again been ahead of a and then comes to be behind it. Conduct before the window behind is not read: a pass that takes longer than the window is not recognized. It denotes the relative motion of the two road users only: it says nothing of the lanes they occupy, of whether b moves, or of why a passes. Not denoted: a drawing alongside b that does not clear b; b ahead of a only while their headings are not aligned (a road user met head-on or crossing); b behind a at every observation of the window.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"a","sort":"track"},{"name":"b","sort":"track"}],"params":[{"name":"window","unit":"s","meaning":"the longest duration of a pass the concept recognizes: how far behind the observation it looks for b ahead of a"},{"name":"same_dir_cos","unit":"ratio","meaning":"cosine of the largest heading difference at which a and b count as travelling in the same direction"}],"act":{"boundary":"window","window":"window","onset":"The act begins at the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of a with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction).","recognition":"The act is recognized at the observation at which b is behind a and was not behind a at the previous observation, where b was ahead of a with headings aligned at some observation of the window behind.","extent":"The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until b has again been ahead of a and then comes to be behind it.","history":"Conduct before the window behind is not read: a pass that takes longer than the window is not recognized."},"elements":[{"span":"the longitudinal component of b's bearing in a's frame (rel.bearing)","atoms":["rel.bearing"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.bearing: 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for \"on the right of\", \"immediately to the rear\")'; its longitudinal component's sign tells b ahead of a from b behind it."},{"span":"the two bodies' projections on a's heading share no length (rel.longitudinal_overlap negative)","atoms":["rel.longitudinal_overlap"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.longitudinal_overlap: 'the length the two footprints' projections on that axis share, negative for the gap between the projections'; a negative value means the bodies are not side by side, so a has cleared b (or not yet reached it). Used as a projection, not as a contact or a distance."},{"span":"with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction)","atoms":["rel.same_direction"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.same_direction: 'headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance', with the tolerance same_dir_cos; it tells an overtaking from a meeting or a crossing."}],"residues":[],"literals":[],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"a follows b in the same lane 15 m behind at 12 m/s while b is halted; a moves to the adjacent lane, draws alongside and, 4 s after b was last ahead of it, has b 3 m behind it: at that observation the concept holds."},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"a follows b, moves to the adjacent lane and draws alongside b, then halts with the two bodies still side by side; b never comes to be behind a within the window."},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"a draws past b in the adjacent lane, but the bearing of b from a is not observed.","masked":["rel.bearing"]}],"used_by":["LVMC_11_30_030"],"supersedes":null}

{"concept_id":"drv.motion.moving_across_carrier","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user a moves across the designated direction of travel of carrier region r: a is moving, its speed (kin.speed) above speed_tol, and its velocity (kin.velocity) makes with r's designated direction (st.lane_direction) an angle whose cosine, in absolute value, is at most cos_max: the absolute value of the dot product of the velocity with the normalised direction is at most cos_max times the speed. Either sense of crossing is denoted: the sign of the direction does not matter. It is a state at one observation: it says nothing of whether a occupies r, of where a began or will end its movement, or of how long it has moved so. Not denoted: a road user at rest or moving at or below speed_tol; a road user moving more nearly along r's direction than cos_max allows. {"concept_id":"drv.interaction.overtake_pass","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear: a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it. b is ahead of a where the longitudinal component of b's bearing in a's frame (rel.bearing) is positive and the two bodies' projections on a's heading share no length (rel.longitudinal_overlap negative); b is behind a where that component is negative and the projections share no length. The act begins at the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of a with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction). The act is recognized at the observation at which b is behind a and was not behind a at the previous observation, where b was ahead of a with headings aligned at some observation of the window behind. The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until b has again been ahead of a and then comes to be behind it. Conduct before the window behind is not read: a pass that takes longer than the window is not recognized. It denotes the relative motion of the two road users only: it says nothing of the lanes they occupy, of whether b moves, or of why a passes. {"concept_id":"drv.interaction.overtake_pass","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear: a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it. b is ahead of a where the longitudinal component of b's bearing in a's frame (rel.bearing) is positive and the two bodies' projections on a's heading share no length (rel.longitudinal_overlap negative); b is behind a where that component is negative and the projections share no length. Conduct before the window behind is not read: a pass that takes longer than the window is not recognized. It denotes the relative motion of the two road users only: it says nothing of the lanes they occupy, of whether b moves, or of why a passes. {"concept_id":"drv.interaction.overtake_pass","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear: a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it. b is ahead of a where the longitudinal component of b's bearing in a's frame (rel.bearing) is positive and the two bodies' projections on a's heading share no length (rel.longitudinal_overlap negative); b is behind a where that component is negative and the projections share no length. The act begins at the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of a with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction). The act is recognized at the observation at which b is behind a and was not behind a at the previous observation, where b was ahead of a with headings aligned at some observation of the window behind. The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until b has again been ahead of a and then comes to be behind it. Conduct before the window behind is not read: a pass that takes longer than the window is not recognized. It denotes the relative motion of the two road users only: it says nothing of the lanes they occupy, of whether b moves, or of why a passes. Not denoted: a drawing alongside b that does not clear b; b ahead of a only while their headings are not aligned (a road user met head-on or crossing); b behind a at every observation of the window.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"a","sort":"track"},{"name":"b","sort":"track"}],"params":[{"name":"window","unit":"s","meaning":"the longest duration of a pass the concept recognizes: how far behind the observation it looks for b ahead of a"},{"name":"same_dir_cos","unit":"ratio","meaning":"cosine of the largest heading difference at which a and b count as travelling in the same direction"}],"act":{"boundary":"window","window":"window","onset":"The act begins at the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of a with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction).","recognition":"The act is recognized at the observation at which b is behind a and was not behind a at the previous observation, where b was ahead of a with headings aligned at some observation of the window behind.","extent":"The concept holds at that observation only, and not again until b has again been ahead of a and then comes to be behind it.","history":"Conduct before the window behind is not read: a pass that takes longer than the window is not recognized."},"elements":[{"span":"the longitudinal component of b's bearing in a's frame (rel.bearing)","atoms":["rel.bearing"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.bearing: 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for \"on the right of\", \"immediately to the rear\")'; its longitudinal component's sign tells b ahead of a from b behind it."},{"span":"the two bodies' projections on a's heading share no length (rel.longitudinal_overlap negative)","atoms":["rel.longitudinal_overlap"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.longitudinal_overlap: 'the length the two footprints' projections on that axis share, negative for the gap between the projections'; a negative value means the bodies are not side by side, so a has cleared b (or not yet reached it). Used as a projection, not as a contact or a distance."},{"span":"with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction)","atoms":["rel.same_direction"],"concepts":[],"justification":"rel.same_direction: 'headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance', with the tolerance same_dir_cos; it tells an overtaking from a meeting or a crossing."}],"residues":[],"literals":[],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"a follows b in the same lane 15 m behind at 12 m/s while b is halted; a moves to the adjacent lane, draws alongside and, 4 s after b was last ahead of it, has b 3 m behind it: at that observation the concept holds."},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"a follows b, moves to the adjacent lane and draws alongside b, then halts with the two bodies still side by side; b never comes to be behind a within the window."},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"a draws past b in the adjacent lane, but the bearing of b from a is not observed.","masked":["rel.bearing"]}],"used_by":["LVMC_11_30_030"],"supersedes":null}

{"concept_id":"drv.motion.moving_across_carrier","kind":"formula","contract":"Road user a moves across the designated direction of travel of carrier region r: a is moving, its speed (kin.speed) above speed_tol, and its velocity (kin.velocity) makes with r's designated direction (st.lane_direction) an angle whose cosine, in absolute value, is at most cos_max: the absolute value of the dot product of the velocity with the normalised direction is at most cos_max times the speed. Either sense of crossing is denoted: the sign of the direction does not matter. It is a state at one observation: it says nothing of whether a occupies r, of where a began or will end its movement, or of how long it has moved so. Not denoted: a road user at rest or moving at or below speed_tol; a road user moving more nearly along r's direction than cos_max allows. Where r carries no designated direction, or a's velocity is not observed, it is unknown.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"a","sort":"track"},{"name":"r","sort":"region"}],"params":[{"name":"speed_tol","unit":"m/s","meaning":"the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement"},{"name":"cos_max","unit":"ratio","meaning":"the largest absolute cosine between the velocity and the carrier's designated direction at which the motion counts as across the carrier"}],"elements":[{"span":"its speed (kin.speed) above speed_tol","atoms":["kin.speed"],"concepts":[],"justification":"kin.speed: 'magnitude of velocity' (m/s); above speed_tol the road user is moving."},{"span":"its velocity (kin.velocity)","atoms":["kin.velocity"],"concepts":[],"justification":"kin.velocity: 'velocity vector' (m/s, world frame); its dot product with the direction gives the motion along the carrier."},{"span":"r's designated direction (st.lane_direction)","atoms":["st.lane_direction"],"concepts":[],"justification":"st.lane_direction: 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in — a lane, ... or a roadway', read normalised; a place no carrier covers has none (unknown)."}],"residues":[],"literals":[],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A pedestrian on a lane whose direction is east walks north at 1.4 m/s: the dot product is zero, at most cos_max times the speed."},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"A pedestrian on the same lane walks east along it at 1.4 m/s: the absolute cosine is 1, above cos_max."},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"A pedestrian on the lane moves, but its velocity is not observed.","masked":["kin.velocity"]}],"used_by":["LVMC_11_30_050","LVMC_11_30_060_A","LVMC_11_30_060_B"],"supersedes":null}

# Plan — iter-001, batch 02

Eight laws, eight nodes, two new concept records (`drv.interaction.overtake_pass`,
`drv.motion.moving_across_carrier`). `drv.motion.complete_halt`, proposed earlier in this iteration,
is reused unchanged. Five nodes carry no gap and can be coded. Three carry gaps and stay blocked:
LVMC_11_22_100, LVMC_11_22_120_B and LVMC_11_27_010_A. No law-local aggregates
(`aggregates.jsonl` is empty). The validator accepts every node and both concepts.

## LVMC_11_22_020 — careless or imprudent driving (surrogate)
The whole duty is a standard of care, so the node is marked **surrogate**. "careless or imprudent
manner" is operationalized by the traffic-conflict technique. While the subject vehicle moves on a
highway in the City, it must not touch another road user (`rel.contact`). Nor may it have a projected
closest approach within `p.conflict_horizon` at a centre distance below `p.conflict_centre_clearance`.
Both parameters are re-proposed with the values LVMC_11_12_070_B gave them. "drive or operate" is
read through controlled motion (agency). "on any highway" reuses the index mapping
(`rel.occupies`, `st.highway`). "in the City" is a city limit, which is a legal region class, so it is
the new assumption `asm.within_city_limits`. *Reversal signal:* operator review classifies a careless
manoeuvre with no conflict (e.g. weaving alone on the road) as a violation. That would require more
factors in the operationalization.

## LVMC_11_22_100 — new pavement or closed street (gapped)
The duty: do not drive over pavement newly laid or repaired that a barricade, a flagger or warning
sign, or a "highway closed" sign marks. The marks map to existing atoms through `dev.governs`:
- the barricade to `dev.temporary_traffic_control`;
- the flagger or warning sign to `dev.human_direction`, `dev.temporary_traffic_control` and
  `dev.regulatory_sign`;
- the closed sign to `dev.regulatory_sign` code `closed_to_traffic`.

"pavement newly laid or repaired" has no atom. The duty turns on it, so it is the atom gap
`st.fresh_pavement`. The exception for "employees actually engaged in the paving or repair" turns on
the work a road user is doing. The validator rejected reading it through the `ru.official_vehicle`
class, so it is the atom gap `ru.road_work_activity`. *Reversal signal:* the operator retires either
gap with an atom, or rules that a works closure (`dev.temporary_traffic_control` governing a region)
may stand for the fresh pavement.

## LVMC_11_22_120_B — nonmotorized-traffic street closures (gapped)
The obligation is the second sentence: disobeying the posted restriction means using
(`rel.occupies`) a roadway that a restricting sign governs while being of the class the sign
prohibits. The first sentence describes which signs count. The designation by the Traffic Engineer
and "appropriate signs" are read as status through the sign's presence. The listed classes map as:
- bicycles to the admitted aggregate `DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle`;
- other nonmotorized traffic to `DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic` with the nonmotorized qualifier;
- motor-driven cycles to `ru.moped` / `ru.motorcycle` (no definition applies).

There is no class for a horse-drawn vehicle, so the span carries the atom gap `ru.animal_drawn_vehicle`.
The subject is "no person". The index maps "A person" (LVMC_11_22_010) to the vehicle aggregate.
Here the words reach every road user a sign may restrict, pedestrians and bicycles included, so the
subject is the traffic aggregate. *Reversal signal:* the operator adds an animal-drawn-vehicle class.

## LVMC_11_27_010_A — motorized vehicles on trails (gapped)
The subject is the vehicle aggregate. The law's own word "motorized" narrows it to the motorized
classes, which stand beside the aggregate and never replace it. "operate" is read as controlled
motion: the vehicle is moving. The three conditions on the right-of-way map as follows:
- the trails-plan designation and the dedication to the City are legal region classes, so they
  become the assumptions `asm.designated_trail` and `asm.trail_dedicated_to_city`;
- the posting is a `motor_vehicles_prohibited` regulatory sign governing the travel region the
  subject occupies.

The exceptions:
- **Emergency vehicles:** `ru.emergency_vehicle`, the class alone, because the words name the class.
- **Maintenance use:** "being used in connection with maintenance of the right-of-way" is a use. A
  class can't evidence a use, so it carries the gap `ru.road_work_activity`, the same proposal as
  LVMC_11_22_100's.
- **Wheelchairs and mobility devices:** a scope-`none` residue. Such devices carry none of the
  motorized classes the subject must carry, so the duty is the same either way.
- **"Except as otherwise provided in Subsection (B)":** a scope-`none` residue. Subsection (B) is this
  text's own exception list, already carried.

*Reversal signal:* `ru.road_work_activity` is admitted, or the operator rules that maintenance
livery may evidence the use.

## LVMC_11_30_030 — passing a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk
The obligation "approaching from the rear shall not overtake and pass such stopped vehicle" maps to
the new act concept `drv.interaction.overtake_pass(a, b)`. It holds where a, travelling in the same
direction as b, comes from having b ahead (positive bearing, no longitudinal overlap) to having b
behind, within a recognition window. Being an act, it is judged at recognition with window
`p.overtake_window`. The trigger names the stopped vehicle b, the crosswalk (marked, or unmarked at
an intersection — both are `st.crosswalk`) and the pedestrian. It is read `some_moment` while the
pass is under way:
- b is at a complete halt;
- b's body is on the crosswalk or within `p.stop_point_tolerance` of it;
- the crosswalk is not behind b along a carrier it occupies (`prim.region_offset_along`).

"to permit a pedestrian to cross" is a purpose. It is read through the conduct it explains: a
pedestrian occupies that crosswalk. b and the pedestrian are quantified, not bound. *Reversal
signal:* a labelled recording where a halt for a pedestrian still on the curb counts. That would
need the pedestrian's approach to the crosswalk to be read.

## LVMC_11_30_050 — route of crossing a roadway
The new concept `drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(a, r)` is a state of motion at one observation:
the road user moves, and the absolute cosine between its velocity and r's designated direction is at
most `cos_max`. It is used twice:
- "cross a roadway" uses `p.crossing_motion_cos`. It tells crossing from walking along.
- "at right angles to the curb / shortest route to the opposite curb" uses
  `p.right_angle_crossing_cos`. The curb runs with the carrier's direction, and between parallel
  curbs the shortest route is the perpendicular one.

The perpendicular reading is disclosed as a narrowing. A pedestrian inside a crosswalk is excepted.
*Reversal signal:* recordings with unlaned two-way roadways, where the duty reports unknown for lack
of a direction. That would call for a curb-direction atom.

## LVMC_11_30_060_A / LVMC_11_30_060_B — crossing outside a crosswalk / at a grade separation
Both nodes read "crossing a roadway" with the same concept and tolerance as LVMC_11_30_050. Where
they differ:
- (A) applies where the pedestrian occupies no crosswalk.
- (B) applies where a `st.pedestrian_grade_separation` is within `p.grade_separation_reach` of the
  pedestrian (`st.region_geometry`).

"shall yield" reuses the index mapping (`kin.speed`, `rel.contact`). The standard "the right-of-way"
is its definition's danger of a crash from "direction, speed and proximity". It is operationalized,
as in LVMC_11_12_070_B, by the constant-velocity closest approach (`p.conflict_horizon`,
`p.conflict_centre_clearance`). "all vehicles upon the roadway" are quantified on the roadway the
pedestrian crosses, re-bound in the obligation.

The closing sentence names Section 11.30.070. The validator rejects composing it because it is
neither accepted nor planned in this run. So the reference words are a residue, and the exception's
own words, "when pedestrians are prohibited from crossing at certain designated places", are carried
by a `pedestrians_prohibited` regulatory sign governing the roadway (status reading). *Reversal
signal:* LVMC 11.30.070 enters the library. Then the reference becomes an `exception` composition
on that node and replaces the sign reading.

## For the operator
- **Right-of-way in LVMC-11-27-010-A.** The resolved definition, DEF-NRS-484A-210, is the
  precedence right "to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another". The law uses
  "right-of-way" for a strip of land ("upon or within a right-of-way that … has been dedicated to the
  City"), which that definition can't bear. The plan reads the place, carried by occupancy and the
  assumptions. The definition precedence for this law may need review.
- **LVMC 11.30.070 is not in the library.** LVMC_11_30_060_A and LVMC_11_30_060_B read the exception
  only through a posted pedestrian prohibition. If 11.30.070 also prohibits crossing in other places
  (for example between adjacent signalized intersections), those places are not excepted until that
  law is planned and the reference composed.
- **No sign code for motor-driven cycles.** `dev.regulatory_sign` has no code for a prohibition of
  motor-driven cycles. The validator rejects a gap on an existing atom, so it is reported here: once
  LVMC_11_22_120_B is unblocked, a sign prohibiting motor-driven cycles will not engage it.
- **Shared gap.** `ru.road_work_activity` is proposed on two laws, LVMC_11_22_100 a7 and
  LVMC_11_27_010_A c9, with the same row.
- **New parameters.** `p.overtake_window`, `p.overtake_same_direction_cos`, `p.crossing_motion_cos`,
  `p.right_angle_crossing_cos` and `p.grade_separation_reach` are proposed with provisional values
  for review. `p.halt_speed_tolerance`, `p.stop_point_tolerance`, `p.conflict_horizon` and
  `p.conflict_centre_clearance` are re-proposed with the values already given this iteration.

# Plan — iter-001, batch 02

Eight laws, eight nodes, two new concept records (`drv.interaction.overtake_pass`,
`drv.motion.moving_across_carrier`). `drv.motion.complete_halt`, proposed earlier in this iteration,
is reused unchanged. Five nodes carry no gap and can be coded. Three carry gaps and stay blocked:
LVMC_11_22_100, LVMC_11_22_120_B and LVMC_11_27_010_A. No law-local aggregates
(`aggregates.jsonl` is empty). The validator accepts every node and both concepts.

## LVMC_11_22_020 — careless or imprudent driving (surrogate)
The whole duty is a standard of care, so the node is marked **surrogate**. "careless or imprudent
manner" is operationalized by the traffic-conflict technique. While the subject vehicle moves on a
highway in the City, it must not touch another road user (`rel.contact`). Nor may it have a projected
closest approach within `p.conflict_horizon` at a centre distance below `p.conflict_centre_clearance`.
Both parameters are re-proposed with the values LVMC_11_12_070_B gave them. "drive or operate" is
read through controlled motion (agency). "on any highway" reuses the index mapping
(`rel.occupies`, `st.highway`). "in the City" is a city limit, which is a legal region class, so it is
the new assumption `asm.within_city_limits`. *Reversal signal:* operator review classifies a careless
manoeuvre with no conflict (e.g. weaving alone on the road) as a violation. That would require more
factors in the operationalization.

## LVMC_11_22_100 — new pavement or closed street (gapped)
The duty: do not drive over pavement newly laid or repaired that a barricade, a flagger or warning
sign, or a "highway closed" sign marks. The marks map to existing atoms through `dev.governs`:
- the barricade to `dev.temporary_traffic_control`;
- the flagger or warning sign to `dev.human_direction`, `dev.temporary_traffic_control` and
  `dev.regulatory_sign`;
- the closed sign to `dev.regulatory_sign` code `closed_to_traffic`.

"pavement newly laid or repaired" has no atom. The duty turns on it, so it is the atom gap
`st.fresh_pavement`. The exception for "employees actually engaged in the paving or repair" turns on
the work a road user is doing. The validator rejected reading it through the `ru.official_vehicle`
class, so it is the atom gap `ru.road_work_activity`. *Reversal signal:* the operator retires either
gap with an atom, or rules that a works closure (`dev.temporary_traffic_control` governing a region)
may stand for the fresh pavement.

## LVMC_11_22_120_B — nonmotorized-traffic street closures (gapped)
The obligation is the second sentence: disobeying the posted restriction means using
(`rel.occupies`) a roadway that a restricting sign governs while being of the class the sign
prohibits. The first sentence describes which signs count. The designation by the Traffic Engineer
and "appropriate signs" are read as status through the sign's presence. The listed classes map as:
- bicycles to the admitted aggregate `DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle`;
- other nonmotorized traffic to `DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic` with the nonmotorized qualifier;
- motor-driven cycles to `ru.moped` / `ru.motorcycle` (no definition applies).

There is no class for a horse-drawn vehicle, so the span carries the atom gap `ru.animal_drawn_vehicle`.
The subject is "no person". The index maps "A person" (LVMC_11_22_010) to the vehicle aggregate.
Here the words reach every road user a sign may restrict, pedestrians and bicycles included, so the
subject is the traffic aggregate. *Reversal signal:* the operator adds an animal-drawn-vehicle class.

## LVMC_11_27_010_A — motorized vehicles on trails (gapped)
The subject is the vehicle aggregate. The law's own word "motorized" narrows it to the motorized
classes, which stand beside the aggregate and never replace it. "operate" is read as controlled
motion: the vehicle is moving. The three conditions on the right-of-way map as follows:
- the trails-plan designation and the dedication to the City are legal region classes, so they
  become the assumptions `asm.designated_trail` and `asm.trail_dedicated_to_city`;
- the posting is a `motor_vehicles_prohibited` regulatory sign governing the travel region the
  subject occupies.

The exceptions:
- **Emergency vehicles:** `ru.emergency_vehicle`, the class alone, because the words name the class.
- **Maintenance use:** "being used in connection with maintenance of the right-of-way" is a use. A
  class can't evidence a use, so it carries the gap `ru.road_work_activity`, the same proposal as
  LVMC_11_22_100's.
- **Wheelchairs and mobility devices:** a scope-`none` residue. Such devices carry none of the
  motorized classes the subject must carry, so the duty is the same either way.
- **"Except as otherwise provided in Subsection (B)":** a scope-`none` residue. Subsection (B) is this
  text's own exception list, already carried.

*Reversal signal:* `ru.road_work_activity` is admitted, or the operator rules that maintenance
livery may evidence the use.

## LVMC_11_30_030 — passing a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk
The obligation "approaching from the rear shall not overtake and pass such stopped vehicle" maps to
the new act concept `drv.interaction.overtake_pass(a, b)`. It holds where a, travelling in the same
direction as b, comes from having b ahead (positive bearing, no longitudinal overlap) to having b
behind, within a recognition window. Being an act, it is judged at recognition with window
`p.overtake_window`. The trigger names the stopped vehicle b, the crosswalk (marked, or unmarked at
an intersection — both are `st.crosswalk`) and the pedestrian. It is read `some_moment` while the
pass is under way:
- b is at a complete halt;
- b's body is on the crosswalk or within `p.stop_point_tolerance` of it;
- the crosswalk is not behind b along a carrier it occupies (`prim.region_offset_along`).

"to permit a pedestrian to cross" is a purpose. It is read through the conduct it explains: a
pedestrian occupies that crosswalk. b and the pedestrian are quantified, not bound. *Reversal
signal:* a labelled recording where a halt for a pedestrian still on the curb counts. That would
need the pedestrian's approach to the crosswalk to be read.

## LVMC_11_30_050 — route of crossing a roadway
The new concept `drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(a, r)` is a state of motion at one observation:
the road user moves, and the absolute cosine between its velocity and r's designated direction is at
most `cos_max`. It is used twice:
- "cross a roadway" uses `p.crossing_motion_cos`. It tells crossing from walking along.
- "at right angles to the curb / shortest route to the opposite curb" uses
  `p.right_angle_crossing_cos`. The curb runs with the carrier's direction, and between parallel
  curbs the shortest route is the perpendicular one.

The perpendicular reading is disclosed as a narrowing. A pedestrian inside a crosswalk is excepted.
*Reversal signal:* recordings with unlaned two-way roadways, where the duty reports unknown for lack
of a direction. That would call for a curb-direction atom.

## LVMC_11_30_060_A / LVMC_11_30_060_B — crossing outside a crosswalk / at a grade separation
Both nodes read "crossing a roadway" with the same concept and tolerance as LVMC_11_30_050. Where
they differ:
- (A) applies where the pedestrian occupies no crosswalk.
- (B) applies where a `st.pedestrian_grade_separation` is within `p.grade_separation_reach` of the
  pedestrian (`st.region_geometry`).

"shall yield" reuses the index mapping (`kin.speed`, `rel.contact`). The standard "the right-of-way"
is its definition's danger of a crash from "direction, speed and proximity". It is operationalized,
as in LVMC_11_12_070_B, by the constant-velocity closest approach (`p.conflict_horizon`,
`p.conflict_centre_clearance`). "all vehicles upon the roadway" are quantified on the roadway the
pedestrian crosses, re-bound in the obligation.

The closing sentence names Section 11.30.070. The validator rejects composing it because it is
neither accepted nor planned in this run. So the reference words are a residue, and the exception's
own words, "when pedestrians are prohibited from crossing at certain designated places", are carried
by a `pedestrians_prohibited` regulatory sign governing the roadway (status reading). *Reversal
signal:* LVMC 11.30.070 enters the library. Then the reference becomes an `exception` composition
on that node and replaces the sign reading.

## For the operator
- **Right-of-way in LVMC-11-27-010-A.** The resolved definition, DEF-NRS-484A-210, is the
  precedence right "to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another". The law uses
  "right-of-way" for a strip of land ("upon or within a right-of-way that … has been dedicated to the
  City"), which that definition can't bear. The plan reads the place, carried by occupancy and the
  assumptions. The definition precedence for this law may need review.
- **LVMC 11.30.070 is not in the library.** LVMC_11_30_060_A and LVMC_11_30_060_B read the exception
  only through a posted pedestrian prohibition. If 11.30.070 also prohibits crossing in other places
  (for example between adjacent signalized intersections), those places are not excepted until that
  law is planned and the reference composed.
- **No sign code for motor-driven cycles.** `dev.regulatory_sign` has no code for a prohibition of
  motor-driven cycles. The validator rejects a gap on an existing atom, so it is reported here: once
  LVMC_11_22_120_B is unblocked, a sign prohibiting motor-driven cycles will not engage it.
- **Shared gap.** `ru.road_work_activity` is proposed on two laws, LVMC_11_22_100 a7 and
  LVMC_11_27_010_A c9, with the same row.
- **New parameters.** `p.overtake_window`, `p.overtake_same_direction_cos`, `p.crossing_motion_cos`,
  `p.right_angle_crossing_cos` and `p.grade_separation_reach` are proposed with provisional values
  for review. `p.halt_speed_tolerance`, `p.stop_point_tolerance`, `p.conflict_horizon` and
  `p.conflict_centre_clearance` are re-proposed with the values already given this iteration.

- **`LVMC_11_30_060_A` and `LVMC_11_30_060_B`** (pedestrian yields when crossing outside a crosswalk, or near a pedestrian tunnel or overpass): "yield the right-of-way" is read as not walking into a projected near-collision with a vehicle on that roadway.

**Blocked by gaps:**
- **`LVMC_11_22_100`:** nothing in the ontology marks pavement as "newly laid or repaired" (`st.fresh_pavement`). Nothing records that a road user is "actually engaged" in the paving either (`ru.road_work_activity`).
- **`LVMC_11_22_120_B`:** there is no class for horse-drawn vehicles (`ru.animal_drawn_vehicle`).
- **`LVMC_11_27_010_A`:** the maintenance-vehicle exception turns on what a vehicle is being used for, which a vehicle class can't show. It carries the same `ru.road_work_activity` gap.

**For you to look at** (details in `PLAN.md` under "For the operator"):
- **Section 11.30.070 isn't in the library**, so the validator won't let me compose it into the two 060 rules. I carried their exception only through a posted "pedestrians prohibited" sign. Any other place 11.30.070 prohibits crossing isn't excepted until that law is planned.
- **The applicable "right-of-way" definition doesn't fit 11.27.010(A).** It defines a right to proceed first, but the law uses the word for a strip of land. I read it as the place.
- **There's no sign code for a motor-driven-cycle prohibition.** The validator rejected a gap on an existing atom, so this is recorded only in `PLAN.md`. Even once unblocked, `LVMC_11_22_120_B` won't apply to such a sign.
- **Five new parameters** have provisional values for review: overtake window, overtake heading tolerance, two crossing-angle tolerances, and the reach around a pedestrian tunnel or overpass.

Files are in `iter-001/plan/batch-02/`:
- `blueprint.jsonl`
- `PLAN.md`
- `aggregates.jsonl` (empty, since none of these laws defines its own class of road users)
